chunks: Sahl, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

It is as if I am with Al-Qaim (peace be upon him) upon the pulpit of Kufa, wearing a gown; he takes out from the fold of his gown a book sealed with a gold seal, unties it, and reads it to the people. They flee from him as sheep flee, so none remain except the commanders. He speaks a speech, and they do not find a refuge until they return to him. And I know the speech that he will speak.

key_terms.إِجْفَالَ: Fleeing or running away in fear
key_terms.النُّقَبَاء: The commanders or leaders (often referring to the elite or military leaders)
key_terms.الْقَائِم: Al-Qaim (The Riser), a title for the Twelfth Imam
key_terms.قَبَاءٌ: A loose outer garment or gown
key_terms.مِنْبَرِ الْكُوفَةِ: The Pulpit of Kufa, a significant location for the Imam's declaration
key_terms.وَرَيَان: The fold or pleat of a garment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the appearance and actions of Al-Qaim on the pulpit of Kufa?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the eschatological authority of the Twelfth Imam, Al-Qaim, who will emerge in Kufa to reveal a sealed book, likely the Quran or a specific divine decree, causing the masses to flee in awe while the elite commanders remain. The Imam’s intimate knowledge of the specific speech underscores his unique role as the ultimate interpreter of divine will, a theme central to Shia eschatology regarding the establishment of justice. The imagery of the golden seal and the sealed book reflects the preservation of authentic tradition against the distortions of the preceding eras.
